challenge.better_approach: The two offered options measured short. (a) Running only the proofs whose subject changed is already in force: b0e65's 54 runs were all moved-closure seals, 51 of them via tester/device.py (fdcf52ae0, ticket 73caa3ab76f6, not resealed). (b) Bounded parallel workers are floored by the 1040.8 s proof and serialize at the tester's shim lock, since _handle_run runs run_proof synchronously under it; lifting that is a tester change, out of bounds. Reading the seal is the cheaper and reproducible lever constrain owns.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That an unknown 'seal moved' is enough for the chart to judge bounds. The build reseals at PROVEME anyway, so the measured verdict arrives there.
challenge.prior_art: 070c5fc9624c shares the run cache across firings; it cut repeat cost, not first cost. standing() exists in cairn.tools.base.validation and the floor already uses it for proven seals.
challenge.real_collision: test_chart_constrain.py teeth test_a_named_check_is_never_reported_unrun and test_one_red_check_does_not_blanket_the_report require the floor to RUN an unsealed planted proof and say red. A seal-read floor reports it never-sealed. The why of those teeth is that a report never defaults to green, and a never-sealed state still is not green, but the teeth as written would change. That needs a ruling, not a quiet rewrite.

answers.falsifier: Done when the floor over cairn/devices/tester at e1d7881233e6 asks the tester zero times and finishes in seconds, reporting 7 green and 54 moved with their files, and two firings agree. Wrong intent if a chart stage must know whether an unsealed proof passes today, not only that its seal moved.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator asked for it from b0e65cf8a77e's measured constrain cost (run_cache on akiendelllinux, copied to the scratchpad b0e65/), recorded on ticket d58e7887cc99 (CairnCommons/tickets/d58e7887cc99-constrain-s-floor-waits-the-stage-budget-for-the-tester.json)
answers.how: _run_instrument reads standing(abs_path): proven is green, as today. Moved, red and never-sealed are no longer asked of the tester; each is reported with its standing state and, for moved, the closure files whose bytes changed, and floor_packet carries it as an unknown. The tester ask, the run cache and its flock go. Held for the orchestrator's ruling before BUILDME, because it collides with test_chart_constrain's two teeth that plant an unsealed failing proof and require 'red'.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (a seal already measured is not re-derived inside a chart stage); Law 3 (an unsealed proof is reported as unmeasured, not run into a verdict the floor cannot reproduce); outline 3.3.4.3.
answers.what: constrain's floor reports each instrument's state from its seal (standing) and never runs a proof inside a chart stage, so a floor costs seconds and two firings over the same bytes agree, while a seal that moved rides out as an unknown naming the files that moved.

bullets.text: b0e65's 56-minute floor was not caused by missing a changed-subject filter: that filter is in force, and the run came from an unresealed tester edit moving 51 seals. Parallel runs would serialize at the tester's shim lock anyway. The cheap, reproducible floor reads seals and never runs proofs.
